newsitem.title: USA: Enron sees competition spreading rapidly.
newsitem.headline: Enron sees competition spreading rapidly.

text.p: At least 50 percent of U.S. electric consumers will be free to choose their power suppliers within three or four years, Enron Corp President Jeffrey Skilling said on Thursday.

At a Bloomberg Energy Day forum, Skilling said the restructuring of the industry was proceeding faster than anybody had expected a couple years ago. All customers in Massachusetts and California are now scheduled to select their power supplier by January 1, 1998, he said, though that date "may be delayed until July 1."

Skilling said a quarter to a third of the U.S. electric power market, worth about $200 billion a year, was a natural monopoly and would continue to be regulated. The remainder will be open to competition, which is likely to be brutal, he said.
Skilling said most current integrated utilities were likely to remain in the regulated wires business -- the transmission and distribution of power. "That's the direction I'd go," he said.
However, the allowed return on equity for wire assets "may go down" from what regulators now allow for integrated utilities, as the business will be less risky, he said.
Noting generation will be "totally commodity," he said it "will have all the problems of commodity chemicals with none of the redeeming characteristics."
The survivors will be "highly specialized," he added.
He said Enron this year would sell $3.0 billion to $4.0 billion of electricity, compared with $15 million sold in 1994. ((-- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710.))
